label: Q-01
severityRationale:
MOVED to QA. The deduplicator flagged this for a Low-vs-QA re-weigh and named it the weakest of the eight; that re-weigh resolves DOWNWARD.

Nothing here is a defect in shipped behaviour. The three UniboostStakerV2 instances are correct contracts in a correct-but-unseeded state on a throwaway chain: setDepletionWindow(12) against a zero budget is INERT (rate 0, windowEnd = now+365d, verified), nothing is bricked, nothing is stranded, and the state SELF-HEALS on the first hook.pull(). There is no lost detector - unlike CAND-01, no assertion capability disappeared; a fixture is simply unseeded. C4 reserves Low for state-handling and spec-deviation issues in the code under review; a non-representative local fixture that corrects itself on first use is informational, and C4 explicitly discourages non-critical issues at Low.

It is NOT dropped, and QA is a visible channel (qa-report.md), not a silent set-aside - Law 1 is satisfied. The retention argument the deduplicator made stands and is preserved: it has a concrete, reproducible end state (totalStaked=0, phUSD.balanceOf=0, rewardBudget=0, rewardRate=0 on all three) and a concrete fix. The recommendation is carried verbatim into the QA bundle so the topUp call and the rewardRate > 0 assertion remain actionable - the assertion in particular is the part that makes a future removal fail loudly, and it is worth keeping even though the finding is QA.

recommendation: Either call staker.topUp(REHEARSAL_STAKER_BUDGET) once per staker inside _deployUniboostStaker (the constant already existed at 9563c68), or restore the single index-1 mint so hook.pull() funds them organically. Assert rewardRate > 0 afterwards so a future removal fails loudly.
